children: Gold prices fall in early trading as investors digest the Federal Reserve's policy meeting while waiting for the release of U.S. inflation data later on Thursday. Futures in New York are down 0.2% to $4,045.20 a troy ounce. The U.S. central bank kept rates steady, buying time to decide whether more rate hikes are needed after the midterms. Still, "the tug of war between short-term momentum sellers and longer-term accumulators continues, leaving prices directionless amid concerns over elevated energy prices, AI-related equity weakness, bond yields and the dollar," analysts at Saxo Bank say. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
